messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach on dedicated pool `dedicated-east-1-prod`. Automated check: p99 > 5s for the last 5m. Queue depth trending up. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/1976543210

Jamie (oncall): ack — I'm looking. Paging SRE/infra. Can someone paste the pool status?

Ravi (infra): pulling logs now. initial findings: autoscaler cooldown blocked scale because last manual bump 2m ago. Also observed a batch of large seq-length requests — warmup-heavy.

Carlos (sre): metrics snapshot (last 5m): p95=1.2s -> 2.9s, p99=4.8s -> 6.3s, streaming stalls spike, RPS steady ~420/s. Tail latency looks dominated by cold model warmups + queue amplification.

Ravi (infra): raw pool state:
```
Pool: dedicated-east-1-prod
Active GPUs: 24/24 (hard cap)
Queue depth: 780 (target < 50)
Avg warmup time (new worker): 18s
Autoscale cooldown: 180s remaining
Recent scale attempts: 2 (failed to allocate due to AZ capacity)
```

Ana (product): what's the customer impact? any paying tenants affected?

Support (cs): CS update: 12 tenants showing degraded responses, 3 high-priority customers on pages, total error/timeout rate ~2.2% (up from 0.1%). We're drafting outbound note.

Jamie (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce load on dedicated pool by shifting non-critical traffic to hosted-fallback; 2) manual temporary pool spin-up for warmup; 3) enable model-variant fallback for streaming to avoid heavy decode. Who can execute 1 and 2?

Ana (product): I approve shifting 20% traffic to hosted-fallback. That should reduce pressure while we scale. :white_check_mark:

Ravi (infra): doing manual interventions now. Creating warmup pool and requesting extra capacity from cloud (AZ A). Commands run:
```
# create temp warmup pool (preloads KV and tokenizers)
./infractl create-pool --name=warmup-temp-1976 --gpus=4 --preload-models=gpt-large-quant --region=us-east-1 --tags=warmup,temp
# request manual quota bump (internal ticket)
POST /infra/requests -> {"region":"us-east-1","gpus":4,"reason":"inc-1976543210 warmup pool"}
```

Ravi (infra): note — cloud reports soft capacity in AZ A causing delay allocating more GPUs. If AZ A can't satisfy, we can try AZ C but will take ~90s.

Carlos (sre): I'll flip the routing rule to hosted fallback for 20% of traffic and enable model-variant fallback for streaming. Command:
```
robin route set --pool=hosted-fallback --traffic=20% --selector="non-critical" --reason="latency mitigation inc-1976543210"
feature-flag set streaming.fallback=true --env=prod
```

IncidentBot: Action logged: routing change and feature-flag toggle.

Support (cs): CS to customers: sending templated note to the 3 high-priority tenants with workarounds and ETA ~20-30m.

Jamie (oncall): manual scale worked? update?

Ravi (infra): warmup pool created, preloads started. Autoscaler still constrained in AZ A; manual allocation to AZ C is in progress. Warmup pool once ready will accept preloads; ETA ~90s for GPU attach + 30s for model preload.

Carlos (sre): after routing change p95 dropped from 2.9s -> 1.4s in 1m window. p99 down to ~3.2s. Queue depth down to 420. Still above target but improving.

Jamie (oncall): good. keep monitoring. Carlos — keep the hosted fallback at 20% until p99 < 2.0s for 10 continuous minutes.

Carlos (sre): noted. Setting alert: if p99 < 2s for 10m, then auto rollback route.

Ravi (infra): cloud allocation to AZ C succeeded. we've attached 4 GPUs to warmup-temp-1976 and preloads succeeded: model gpt-large-quant warmed, KV caches primed. Also bumped pool soft cap to 28 while we validate.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Manual capacity attach completed and preloads succeeded.

Carlos (sre): visible improvement: queue depth 140, p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.8s, streaming stalls significantly reduced.

Support (cs): customers acknowledged note; 2 of 3 replied with reduced impact thanks. No data loss reported.

Jamie (oncall): escalation status: elevating to Sev2 due to multi-tenant degradation and partial customer impact. Creating incident ticket INC-1976543210. Assigned to Ravi/Carlos for mitigation, Ana for customer comms, Support to manage outreach. Handoff: my shift ends in 15m; I'll do formal handoff with the oncall in rotation.

Ana (product): will coordinate the postmortem and decide on potential product mitigations (e.g., traffic shaping per-tenant, stricter seq-length limits).

Ravi (infra): temporary config changes to autoscaler: reduce cooldown to 60s and relax AZ affinity to allow cross-AZ allocation while this ticket is open. Commands:
```
./infractl update-autoscaler --pool=dedicated-east-1-prod --cooldown=60 --az-affinity=relaxed --reason="inc-1976543210 emergency"
```

Carlos (sre): added follow-ups in incident ticket: investigate warmup failure modes, prioritize preloading for heavy models, add synthetic seq-length burst tests to CI to catch this.

Jamie (oncall): summary for handoff — timeline + mitigations:
- 0m ALERT: p99 breach (incident-bot)
- +2m Manual routing to hosted-fallback 20% (Carlos)
- +4m Warmup pool created and preloads started (Ravi)
- +8m Cloud attach to AZ C + +4 GPUs (Ravi)
- +11m p99 reduced below 2s, queue depth improving (Carlos)
- Current: Sev2, mitigation stable, customer comms active (Ana/Support)

Jamie (oncall): next steps for follow-up owners: Ravi - root cause (AZ capacity + autoscaler cooldown interaction), Carlos - refine routing playbook and add automatic fallback on p99 threshold, Ana - customer-impact postmortem and comms. Please add estimated ETA for RCA in the ticket.

Support (cs): will keep customers updated. Thanks everyone.

Carlos (sre): closing the active paging loop, keeping monitoring watch set to 1m. Will update ticket with metrics and graphs.

Jamie (oncall): handing off to next oncall (Sam). Sam, I'll DM the quick notes and handover link.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-1976543210 created and assigned. Playbook: dedicated-saturation -> warmup & routing mitigations triggered.

Jamie (oncall): :white_check_mark: Incident stable. Moving to monitoring phase. We will run a postmortem and schedule follow-ups.
